## The rule

A pot's per-role prompt override (`hive_settings` key `promptOverride.<role>`, federated over the
pot peer-log) is **APPENDED after** the generated blueprint persona — it **specializes, it never
replaces** (`getHiveInstancePromptOverride` → `role-launch-spec` appends `inst`; the store's own
comment: *"the override SPECIALIZES … it does not replace the role"*). So an override must contain
**only the pot-specific delta**. The default prompt is the GENERATED chain
(`blueprints/<chain>/prompts/<role>.md` + the spliced sections + the client tooling overlay); a pot
adds its specifics on top. **Generated by default; the override only when a user explicitly authors
one — and even then, only the additive part.**

## The trap (what went wrong)

It is tempting to author an override by copying the whole assembled prompt and tweaking it. That is a
**wholesale snapshot**, and it is wrong two ways:

1. **It duplicates.** The override re-states sections the generated base already supplies (AUTO mode,
   looping, coordination, "Who you are", wire schemas…). The assembled prompt then carries each twice.
2. **It freezes.** The snapshot is a point-in-time copy in PG. When the generated source changes
   (e.g. the `## AUTO mode` clause is reworded/consolidated), the override keeps the **stale** copy
   forever — and because it's appended *last*, the stale version is what the agent reads.

Real incident (2026-06-24): `papercusp/promptOverride.su` was a ~21.6 KB wholesale copy of
`pot-instances/papercup-pot.su.md`. With `su-blueprint-persona` ON, the generated su base is the
*generic* `blueprints/base/prompts/su.md` (which carried no AUTO mode), so **every** Papercusp-specific
section — including a now-stale `## AUTO mode` — was riding the frozen snapshot. A fresh edit to the
canonical AUTO clause never reached the live pot psu, and consolidating AUTO would have produced a
*contradictory double* (fresh generated + stale appended).

## The fix pattern

When you find generic content trapped in an override, **move it to the generated chain and slim the
override to the delta**:

1. **Put the generic/cross-cutting content in the generated base**, authored once. The clean
   mechanism is a render function + a splice marker (mirrors `renderWireSchemasSection` /
   `renderCoordLegend`): e.g. `renderModesPolicy()` in `operating-modes-policy.ts`, spliced at
   `AUTO_MODE_MARKER` by `renderSuPlaybook` / `writeSplicedPlaybook`. Add the marker to the bases that
   should carry it (`blueprints/base/prompts/su.md`, `papercusp-su-engineer.tools.md`,
   `papercusp-su-power.tools.md`). An absent marker is a clean no-op (a base may opt out).
2. **Re-seed the override without the moved content.** `pot-instances/<pot>.<role>.md` is the
   version-controlled SOURCE; the live copy is the federated `promptOverride.<role>` in `hive_settings`
   (they DIVERGE — the file is not auto-synced). Re-seed via the loopback write path:
   `POST /api/agent-mcp/pot-override-set { potSlug, kind:'prompt', name:'<role>', value:<file md> }`
   (an empty value CLEARS it). Verify the PG row updated (`harness_shared.hive_settings`).

## The guard

`hive-override-additive-guard.ts` (the file is still internally named `hive-*`;
only the tool/UX-facing vocabulary re-keyed to "Pot" — `additiveOverrideWarning(md)`) detects the smell — an override that
re-states a base-owned section heading or embeds a `PAPERCUSP-SU:` splice marker — and the
`pot-override-set` route surfaces it as a **non-blocking warning** (overrides are the owner's to
author; we flag, we don't gate). If you're adding a new generic section to the base, add its heading to
`BASE_OWNED_HEADINGS` so the guard keeps catching copies of it.

## Why it's not flag- or materialization-sensitive

The su prompt is assembled by `renderSuPlaybook` on **both** paths — `su-blueprint-persona` OFF (base =
`papercusp-su-engineer.tools.md`) and ON (base = the generic `blueprints/base/prompts/su.md`) — so the
marker belongs in whichever base a path uses. Prompt files resolve from the integration/staging tree
(`promptHarnessRoot` → `PAPERCUSP_PROMPT_ROOT`/`PAPERCUSP_INTEGRATION_ROOT`, else `harnessRoot()` =
`libs/papercusp/packages/harness`), so editing the canonical `libs/` source goes live for new sessions
without a release. The `.papercusp/.materialized/` + desktop `sidecar/harness/` copies are generated
artifacts — they regenerate from `libs/` at build; don't hand-edit them.
